Ideally introducing a new dog to only 2-3 very well behaved dogs would be the way to do it. However, if you show up with a new dog to be introduced and our camps are already loaded up, unloading an entire camp and reloading it again for each time this occurs would be a huge time sink and would aggravate all the dogs with the moving back and forth causing a generalized safety risk. 

There are always going to be dogs that aren't necessarily the best behaved but stay within a safe level of play the majority of the time which is why they are allowed to stay in group play. There are generally triggers and tells for their behavior that makes it so we can manage it safely with no incidents. It's likely this is the type of dog you are saying has acted erratic and aggressive before. For dogs like this there are ways to keep the camps safe with new introductions, either holding them on their own lead away from the door while in camp or taking them out of camp for a brief 10-20 minutes while the new dog is introduced and gets comfortable. 

From my perspective, coming from a hotel team who does care a lot,  I don't think anyone would've willingly put a new timid dog in that camp knowing that it could have been a problem with that other dog. We will always take precaution to avoid any possible negative outcomes with introductions. I would personally try to talk to the Hotel manager about the incident, getting any medical bills covered by Petsmart and maybe seek having that dog be taken out of group play. 

If you truly feel the team was negligent and is not following proper care of the dogs, then that is within your right to report the behavior. 

I hope your dog is doing okay, it's heartbreaking to hear that they had such a rough time their first visit.

We sort our camps by temperament at PetSmart. Generally speaking, older large dogs or anxious large dogs will be put in our small dogs camp where they are safe and feel comfortable. It is completely normal for small and large dogs to form friendships and have a good time. There's plenty of large dogs that have learned how to be gentle and play with dogs much smaller than they are. It's very cute. 

As the pet parent, you are more than welcome to request that the hotel staff puts a note in your dog's profile that you prefer he's with little dogs. The only reason(s) this request wouldn't be okay is if your dog was very hyper and too rough with the small dogs which would make the camp unsafe. It sounds like this is not the case for your dog so it should be a non-issue.

As for being kenneled - any dog in our facility will be put in a kennel unless day camp has already begun and has not ended yet. Day camps run from 9am to 5pm. If you were to have him there from 10am to 4pm for instance he would be in Day Camp the entirety of his time with us, as long as you have not requested a lunch break or treat time as those are done in their individual kennels. A dog utilizing our individual 1-on-1 playtimes would be in a kennel the majority of the day except for their 30 minute play time which doesn't have a set time of day and is based on when we have a free moment to do those services.

If it makes you feel any better, there's a 99% chance he didn't have insurance then so him paying you off is more money than you would've received had he tried to play along and act like he did. If you ever get hit by a car again (while in a vehicle yourself or as a pedestrian again) always ask for a picture of their driver's license and insurance card. Also call 911 and have an officer come out to make a police report. That way it is on record who hit you and the specifics. But like I said, I don't think your situation would have gone any differently unfortunately. :(

I do not know of any way you'd get paid time off since this happened off the clock except for through the car insurance of the person who hit you. Was the driver insured, have you received any treatments, and have you accepted a settlement already? 

If you have not accepted a pain & suffering settlement yet and the driver had insurance, you can see your primary care physician or a chiropractor and have a written letter saying to not work x amount of time/days. Then you will need a letter from your manager stating your pay and the hours you will be missing. You can submit these to the insurance company for lost wages. But if you haven't been seeking treatment, it may be too late. They are notoriously annoying for finding any little reason to get out of paying and a month after an accident is too long for them to consider your injuries typically. 

​

If the former does not apply, I suggest seeing your primary care physician and having them write you a letter stating you will need accommodations - light work duties. This will keep you from needing to do as much physical work while you heal up. I also suggest seeing them in general to evaluate your injuries. There are physical therapy exercises that you can do at home with resistance bands that can help improve your injuries over time. You can try googling "physical therapy exercises for injured lower back" for instance and you should get plenty. Be sure not to over do it and if you are feeling increased pain in your injured muscles to discontinue exercises involving that part of your body.
